q: Which cloud model needs no up-front capital expenditure and is owned and run by a provider for many customers?
explanation: A public cloud is owned by the provider (Azure), and you pay as you go with no CapEx.

q: A company must keep customer records in its own datacenter by law, but wants to use Azure for its website. Which model fits?
explanation: Some workloads stay on-premises and some run in Azure, so this is hybrid.

q: Buying ten new servers for your office is an example of…
explanation: Up-front spending on physical equipment is capital expenditure (CapEx).

q: What does the consumption-based model mean?
options: You pay a fixed yearly fee
You pay only for the resources you use, with no up-front cost
You buy hardware and rent it to Microsoft
You pay per user per month regardless of use
explanation: You pay for what you use, and the cost is OpEx.

q: You run a Windows Server VM in Azure. Who installs the operating system updates?
explanation: A VM is IaaS, so the guest OS is your responsibility.

q: Which responsibility is ALWAYS the customer's, whatever the service type?
explanation: Data, devices, and accounts and identities are always yours, even with SaaS.

q: Your developers want to deploy a web app without managing servers or the OS. Which service type?
explanation: With PaaS (for example App Service), Microsoft runs the OS and you bring your code.

q: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word online) is an example of…
explanation: It is finished software that you just use, so it is SaaS.

q: You need to move existing on-premises servers to Azure as they are, without changing them. Which service type?
explanation: Lift-and-shift onto VMs is IaaS.

q: Adding more VM instances behind a load balancer when traffic rises is called…
explanation: Adding more machines is horizontal scaling, or scaling out.

q: Changing a VM from 2 CPUs to 8 CPUs is…
explanation: Making one machine bigger is vertical scaling, or scaling up.

q: A service that keeps running with minimal downtime, promised as 99.99% uptime, shows which benefit?
explanation: Uptime promised in an SLA is high availability.

q: Your app keeps working after a datacenter fails because it runs in another region. Which benefit?
explanation: Recovering from failures and continuing to work is reliability.

q: Using the pricing calculator to forecast next year's Azure bill supports which benefit?
explanation: Forecasting cost is cost predictability.

q: Which statement about serverless computing is TRUE?
options: You are billed only while your code runs
It always runs on dedicated hardware
explanation: With serverless, the provider manages the servers and you pay per execution.

q: You commit to a VM for 3 years in exchange for a large discount. This is a…
explanation: Reservations (reserved instances) are 1- or 3-year commitments.

q: Which option is cheapest but can be stopped by Azure at any time?
explanation: Spot VMs use spare capacity and can be evicted.

q: You already own Windows Server licences. What lets you use them in Azure to pay less?
explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you reuse existing Windows Server and SQL Server licences.

q: Which is an example of manageability OF the cloud (rather than IN the cloud)?
explanation: Management of the cloud means what happens to your resources: autoscaling, monitoring, templates. The portal, CLI and APIs are how you manage, so they are management in the cloud.

q: Which TWO are true of a private cloud? (Choose two)
options: The organisation has complete control of resources
The organisation buys and maintains the hardware
Anyone can buy services from it
explanation: A private cloud gives full control, but you buy and run the hardware (CapEx).

q: Using both Azure and AWS for different workloads is…
explanation: More than one public provider means multi-cloud.

q: With PaaS, who applies the operating system patches?
explanation: In PaaS, Microsoft manages the OS, which is a security and governance benefit.

q: Which scenario best fits SaaS?
options: Running custom software that needs a specific OS version
Providing company-wide email with no infrastructure to manage
explanation: Finished software such as email, used as-is, is SaaS.

q: Physically separate locations within one Azure region, each with independent power, cooling and networking, are…
explanation: Availability zones are separate datacenters within one region.

q: A region that supports availability zones has at least how many zones?
explanation: There are at least three zones in an enabled region.

q: What is a benefit of region pairs?
options: Planned updates are rolled out to one region of the pair at a time
explanation: Pairs reduce risk: updates go one region at a time, and one region of each pair is recovered first in a large outage.

q: Which is a sovereign region?
explanation: Azure Government and Azure China (run by 21Vianet) are sovereign regions.

q: What is the correct hierarchy from top to bottom?
options: Subscription → Management group → Resource group → Resource
Management group → Subscription → Resource group → Resource
Resource group → Subscription → Management group → Resource
Management group → Resource group → Subscription → Resource
explanation: Management groups contain subscriptions, which contain resource groups, which contain resources.

q: Can a resource group contain another resource group?
explanation: Resource groups cannot be nested. Management groups can (up to 6 levels).

q: A VM can belong to how many resource groups at the same time?
explanation: Each resource is in exactly one resource group, though it can be moved to another.

q: What happens when you delete a resource group?
options: Only the empty group is deleted
All resources inside it are deleted too
Resources move to the default group
It is impossible while it has resources
explanation: Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it. This is why delete locks are useful.

q: Two departments need separate Azure bills. What should you create?
explanation: A subscription is a billing boundary. (Tags can also split costs, but separate invoices come from subscriptions.)

q: You must apply the same policy to 12 subscriptions with the least effort. Where do you assign it?
options: On a management group containing the subscriptions
explanation: Settings on a management group are inherited by every subscription below it.

q: Which service gives a group of identical, load-balanced VMs that scale automatically?
explanation: VM Scale Sets are for identical VMs with autoscaling.

q: Availability sets protect VMs from…
options: Rack (hardware) failures and planned maintenance reboots
explanation: Fault domains cover hardware racks and update domains cover maintenance reboots.

q: In an availability set, what is an update domain?
options: A group of VMs rebooted together during maintenance
A copy of data in another region
explanation: Update domains are rebooted one at a time. Fault domains are about shared power and network.

q: You need to run one container quickly without managing VMs or an orchestrator. Which service?
explanation: ACI is the fastest and simplest way to run a container.

q: Which service orchestrates and manages many containers at scale?
explanation: AKS is Azure's managed Kubernetes service for orchestration.

q: Code must run each time a file is uploaded, and you want to pay only when it runs. Which service?
explanation: Event-driven code billed per execution is Azure Functions.

q: Which service hosts web apps and APIs as PaaS, with autoscale and deployment slots?
explanation: App Service is PaaS web hosting.

q: Remote staff need secure Windows desktops hosted in Azure that they can use from any device. Which service?
explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers hosted Windows desktops and apps.

q: Which is NOT a resource a VM needs?
explanation: A VM needs a size, disks, a network interface, a VNet and an image. Queue storage is for app messages.

q: Two VNets in different regions must communicate privately over Microsoft's network. What do you use?
explanation: VNet peering (global peering across regions) uses Microsoft's backbone.

q: You need a private connection from your office to Azure that does NOT travel over the public internet. Which service?
explanation: ExpressRoute is private through a provider. A VPN is encrypted, but it goes over the internet.

q: One developer's laptop needs an encrypted connection to an Azure VNet. Which option?
explanation: Point-to-site connects a single device.

q: Can you purchase a new domain name directly through Azure DNS?
explanation: No. Azure DNS hosts domains; you buy the name from a registrar (or App Service domains).

q: What does a private endpoint do?
options: Gives a service a public IP
Gives a service a private IP from your VNet so it can be reached without the internet
explanation: A private endpoint is a NIC with a private IP linked to a service through Private Link.

q: Which storage service suits images and videos served by a website?
explanation: Blob storage holds unstructured objects accessed over HTTP.

q: Users need a shared folder they can map as a network drive using SMB. Which service?
explanation: Azure Files provides SMB/NFS file shares.

q: Two parts of an app should exchange messages asynchronously. Which storage service?
explanation: Queue storage holds messages of up to 64 KB.

q: Backups must be kept for 7 years and are almost never read. Waiting hours to retrieve them is acceptable. Cheapest tier?
explanation: Archive is cheapest to store but offline. Reading means rehydrating, which takes hours.

q: At what level can the Archive tier be set?
explanation: Archive is set per blob, never as the account default.

q: Which redundancy keeps 3 copies in a single datacenter?
explanation: LRS is locally redundant: 3 copies in one datacenter, the cheapest option.

q: Data must survive the loss of one datacenter but stay within one region. Which redundancy?
explanation: ZRS copies data across 3 availability zones in the same region.

q: You need to READ data from the secondary region at any time, without a failover. Which option?
explanation: Only the RA- options (RA-GRS, RA-GZRS) let you read the secondary at any time.

q: Which TWO tools copy files to Azure Storage? (Choose two)
explanation: AzCopy (command line) and Storage Explorer (GUI) both move data.

q: You want to keep your on-premises Windows file server but sync it with Azure Files and cache hot files locally. Which tool?
explanation: Azure File Sync syncs both ways and uses cloud tiering.

q: You must move 60 TB to Azure and your internet connection is slow. Which option?
explanation: Data Box is a physical device you ship.

q: Which service discovers and assesses on-premises servers before moving them to Azure?
explanation: Azure Migrate is the hub to discover, assess and migrate.

q: What is the cloud identity service that used to be called Azure Active Directory?
explanation: Azure AD was renamed Microsoft Entra ID.

q: An old app needs LDAP, Kerberos and domain join, but you don't want to run domain controllers. Which service?
explanation: Entra Domain Services provides managed domain features.

q: Users sign in once and can open many apps without signing in again. This is…
explanation: Single sign-on.

q: Which is a passwordless sign-in method?
explanation: FIDO2 keys, Windows Hello for Business and the Authenticator app are passwordless.

q: MFA combines factors from which categories?
explanation: Know (password), have (phone), are (biometric).

q: Partner company staff should access your app using their own work accounts. Which feature?
explanation: External identities let outside users sign in with their own identity.

q: Require MFA only when users sign in from outside the company's country. Which feature?
explanation: Conditional Access acts on signals (location, device, risk) to allow, require MFA or block.

q: Let a user manage VMs in ONE resource group only. What do you use?
options: Azure RBAC role assigned at that resource group
explanation: RBAC assigns a role at a scope, here the resource group.

q: Which is NOT a Zero Trust principle?
options: Trust everything inside the corporate network
explanation: Zero Trust never trusts by network location.

q: In defense in depth, network security groups (NSGs) belong to which layer?
explanation: The network layer limits traffic between resources. DDoS protection is the perimeter layer.

q: Which tool gives a secure score and security recommendations across Azure, on-premises and other clouds?
explanation: Defender for Cloud handles security posture and threat protection. (Advisor has a security category too, but "secure score" points to Defender.)

q: Which TWO services are global, so you don't choose a region for them? (Choose two)
explanation: Entra ID and Azure DNS are global. VMs and storage accounts are regional.

q: Which of these does NOT increase your Azure bill?
explanation: Resource groups are free. Egress, region and size all affect cost.

q: In general, data transferred INTO Azure datacenters is…
explanation: Ingress is generally free; egress is charged.

q: Which tool estimates the monthly cost of resources BEFORE you deploy them?
explanation: The pricing calculator is for planning and creates nothing.

q: Which Azure cost tool has Microsoft retired?
explanation: The Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) calculator has been retired. Use the pricing calculator to estimate costs.

q: Send an email when spending reaches 80% of a monthly budget. Which tool?
explanation: Cost Management has budgets and alerts on actual spend.

q: You want to report costs by department across many resource groups. What do you add to resources?
explanation: Tags (for example dept=finance) let you group costs.

q: Are tags on a resource group automatically inherited by its resources?
explanation: Not by default. Azure Policy can enforce or inherit them.

q: Ensure resources can only be created in West Europe. What do you use?
explanation: Policy enforces rules on resource properties, such as allowed locations.

q: Stop anyone from accidentally deleting a production database, while still allowing configuration changes. What do you use?
explanation: A Delete lock allows read and modify, but not delete.

q: A user with the Owner role tries to delete a resource that has a Delete lock. What happens?
options: It is deleted because Owners bypass locks
It fails until the lock is removed
It moves to the recycle bin
explanation: Locks apply to everyone. The lock must be removed first.

q: A ReadOnly lock allows authorised users to…
options: Read, but not modify or delete
explanation: ReadOnly means read only.

q: Which service discovers and classifies sensitive data across on-premises, multi-cloud and SaaS?
explanation: Purview handles data governance, risk and compliance.

q: A group of Azure Policy definitions assigned together is called…
explanation: A policy initiative is a group of policies.

q: Which tool gives a browser-based, already signed-in shell with Bash or PowerShell?
explanation: Cloud Shell runs in the browser with nothing to install.

q: Manage on-premises servers and Kubernetes clusters in another cloud with Azure Policy and RBAC. Which service?
explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure management beyond Azure.

q: Requests from the portal, Azure CLI and PowerShell are all processed by…
explanation: Every management request goes through ARM.

q: ARM templates are…
explanation: ARM templates are declarative JSON. Bicep is a simpler language that compiles to it.

q: Main benefit of infrastructure as code?
explanation: Code produces the same environment every time and can be version-controlled.

q: Which service gives personalised recommendations to cut cost and improve reliability, security and performance?
explanation: Advisor covers 5 categories: reliability, security, performance, operational excellence, cost.

q: You want to be told when an Azure outage affects the services and regions you use. Which service?
explanation: Service Health gives a personalised view of Azure incidents and maintenance.

q: You want to check whether one of your VMs is currently available. Which feature?
explanation: Resource Health shows the health of individual resources.

q: Write queries over collected log data. Which tool?
explanation: Log Analytics is part of Azure Monitor and uses KQL queries.

q: Monitor a web app's response times, failure rates and dependencies. Which tool?
explanation: Application Insights is application performance monitoring, part of Azure Monitor.

q: Send an SMS when a VM's CPU stays above 90%. Which feature?
options: Azure Monitor alert with an action group
explanation: Monitor alerts fire on conditions, and action groups send the SMS or email.

q: Azure Policy vs Azure RBAC: which statement is correct?
options: Policy controls who can act; RBAC controls resource properties
RBAC controls what users can do; Policy controls what resources may look like
explanation: RBAC is about people's actions. Policy is about resource rules.

q: Which TWO can you use from a script to create Azure resources? (Choose two)
explanation: The CLI (az ...) and PowerShell (New-Az...) are both scriptable.

q: Which statement about Azure Cost Management is TRUE?
options: It estimates costs before you deploy
It shows actual spending and can alert on budgets
explanation: Estimating before deployment is the pricing calculator. Cost Management is about actual spend.

q: Which factor can change the price of the same VM size?
explanation: Prices differ by geography (region).

q: Which is a sustainability-aligned cloud practice?
options: Leave development VMs running all night
Shut down or deallocate resources you are not using
Overprovision resources for peak load all year
explanation: Turning off idle resources and right-sizing cut waste and cost. Scale down when demand drops.

q: A development environment is shut down automatically overnight and at weekends. Which benefit does this mainly support?
explanation: Not running idle resources reduces waste and cost.

q: Reliability is one of the pillars of which Microsoft framework?
explanation: The Azure Well-Architected Framework has reliability as a pillar and also shapes predictability.

q: Which is an example of management IN the cloud?
explanation: The portal, CLI, APIs and PowerShell are how you manage. Autoscale, templates, health monitoring and alerts are management OF the cloud.

q: You already run VMware workloads in a private cloud and want to run them in Azure. Which service helps?
explanation: Azure VMware Solution runs VMware workloads in Azure.

q: Which THREE are always the cloud provider's responsibility? (Choose three)
explanation: Physical datacenter, network and hosts always belong to the provider. Accounts and identities are always yours.

q: Which model lets a private cloud "surge" by temporarily using public cloud resources?
explanation: Hybrid cloud connects private and public so you can burst into public resources.

q: You commit to an hourly spend on compute for 1 or 3 years, with flexibility across compute services. What is this?
explanation: A savings plan commits to an hourly spend. A reservation commits to specific resources.

q: A production database runs 24/7 and its needs are stable. Which pricing option fits best?
explanation: Reservations suit stable, predictable, long-running workloads.

q: Which category gives you prebuilt AI features (language, speech, vision) through APIs?
explanation: Azure AI services are prebuilt capabilities used through APIs.

q: Your team needs to build, train and manage a custom machine learning model. Which service?
explanation: Azure Machine Learning is for custom model development and lifecycle management.

q: Which service provides secure two-way communication between the cloud and IoT devices?
explanation: IoT Hub handles secure bi-directional device communication.

q: You want some workloads to run on devices close to where data is generated. Which service?
explanation: IoT Edge extends cloud capabilities to edge devices.

q: Which service is a simplified SaaS platform for building IoT solutions?
explanation: IoT Central is the SaaS IoT platform.

q: Which service supports generative AI scenarios such as chat and content generation?
explanation: Azure OpenAI Service provides generative AI with built-in security and governance controls.

q: Which feature holds inbound and outbound rules that allow or block traffic by source and destination IP address, port and protocol?
explanation: A network security group (NSG) filters network traffic.

q: Which feature lets resources in a virtual network connect securely to Azure SQL databases and storage accounts with optimal routing?
explanation: Service endpoints link a VNet to these Azure resource types.

q: Which feature lets you control how traffic is directed between subnets?
explanation: Custom route tables and UDRs override the default routing.

q: How many VPN gateways can you deploy in each virtual network?
explanation: Only one VPN gateway per virtual network, though it can connect to multiple locations.

q: Which VPN gateway type do you need for VNet-to-VNet and point-to-site connections?
explanation: Route-based gateways are needed for VNet-to-VNet, point-to-site, multisite and ExpressRoute coexistence.

q: What is a benefit of an Azure DNS alias record set?
options: It updates automatically if the target resource's IP address changes
It lets you buy a domain name
explanation: Alias record sets follow the Azure resource they point to.

q: Which storage account type supports both SMB and NFS file shares?
explanation: Premium file shares support both SMB and NFS.

q: Which is a valid storage account name?
explanation: Names are 3 to 24 characters, lowercase letters and numbers only, and unique across Azure.

q: Which endpoint belongs to Azure Files?
explanation: .file. is Azure Files. .blob. is Blob, .queue. is Queue, .table. is Table.

q: How many copies of your data does Azure Storage always keep in the primary region?
explanation: Data is always replicated three times in the primary region.

q: In geo-redundant storage (GRS), how is the data stored in the secondary region?
explanation: GRS copies asynchronously to the secondary region, which uses LRS.

q: Which access tiers can be set as the default at the storage account level?
explanation: Archive isn't available at the account level. All four can be set per blob.

q: What is the maximum usable capacity of an Azure Data Box device?
explanation: A Data Box has up to 80 terabytes of usable storage.

q: AzCopy synchronisation works in which direction?
explanation: AzCopy sync is one-way. Azure File Sync is bi-directional.

q: Which THREE are passwordless options in Microsoft Entra ID? (Choose three)
explanation: Windows Hello for Business, the Authenticator app and FIDO2 keys are passwordless. A password plus SMS is MFA.

q: Which capability supports Teams shared channels and does NOT create guest users in your directory?
explanation: B2B direct connect uses mutual trust between tenants. B2B collaboration creates guest users.

q: Microsoft Entra External ID for customers was formerly known as…
explanation: External ID for customers is the new name for Azure AD B2C.

q: One role assignment gives a user read access and another gives write access to the same resource group. What can the user do?
explanation: Azure RBAC uses an allow model, so permissions add up.

q: Azure RBAC enforces permissions at the application and data level inside your app.
explanation: No. RBAC covers actions that go through Azure Resource Manager. Application security is up to your app.

q: Which service lets you run domain-joined, group policy and LDAP workloads without managing domain controllers?
explanation: Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services. Microsoft runs the domain controllers.

q: DDoS protection belongs to which defense-in-depth layer?
explanation: DDoS protection and perimeter firewalls are the perimeter layer.

q: Which service stores passwords, connection strings, encryption keys and certificates securely?
explanation: Azure Key Vault is the main service for secrets, keys and certificates.

q: Data moving between a web app and a user's browser is protected by…
explanation: In transit = moving data. At rest = stored data.

q: How can Microsoft Defender for Cloud protect on-premises servers?
options: By moving them to a new region
explanation: Azure Arc extends Defender for Cloud plans to non-Azure machines.

q: What sits at the very top of an Entra tenant's management group hierarchy?
explanation: Every Entra tenant has a single top-level Tenant Root Group.

q: Can a resource group be renamed after it is created?
explanation: No. Resource groups can't be renamed or nested.

q: How many parents can a subscription have in the management group hierarchy?
explanation: Each management group and subscription has only one parent.

q: All Azure services automatically fail over to the paired region.
explanation: No. Not all services replicate or fall back automatically. Some need you to configure recovery.

q: You choose which availability zone a VM runs in. What kind of service is that?
explanation: Zonal services (VMs, managed disks, IP addresses) are pinned to a zone.

q: Which VM family is GPU-enabled?
explanation: N-series is GPU-enabled. D is general purpose, E is memory optimised, B is burstable.

q: Azure Functions are stateless by default. What are the stateful ones called?
explanation: Durable Functions keep state across executions.

q: Which App Service feature runs a program or script in the context of a web app, on a schedule or trigger?
explanation: WebJobs run background tasks alongside your app.

q: Which container service is PaaS and has built-in load balancing and scaling?
explanation: Container Apps add built-in load balancing and scaling. ACI is the simplest way to run one container.

q: Which is true of the Azure free student account?
explanation: The student account gives $100 credit and free developer tools without a credit card.

q: What does the Azure free account include?
options: Popular products free for 12 months, a credit for the first 30 days, and some always-free services
explanation: 12 months of popular products, a 30-day credit and some always-free services.

q: You delete a VM. Which of these may still be billed if you forget about it?
options: Its attached disks and network resources
The name of the resource group
explanation: Deprovisioning a VM does not always remove the extra resources created with it. Check for leftovers to control cost (the maintenance factor).

q: What is a billing zone?
options: A geographic grouping of regions used for data-transfer pricing
A separate datacenter in a region
explanation: Billing zones price outbound data transfer. They are not availability zones.

q: Which is NOT a type of cost alert in Cost Management?
explanation: The three cost alert types are budget, credit and department spending quota.

q: You want to shut down non-production resources automatically when spending reaches a limit. Which feature can trigger that?
explanation: Budgets can trigger automation when a threshold is reached.

q: Which is NOT a typical use of tags?
explanation: Tags are labels. They don't encrypt anything.

q: Microsoft Purview's two main solution areas are…
options: Risk and compliance, and unified data governance
explanation: Purview covers risk and compliance, and unified data governance.

q: Which tool can automatically add a required tag when it is missing from a new resource?
explanation: Azure Policy can remediate non-compliant resources, for example by adding a tag.

q: Where can you find Microsoft's compliance documents and audit reports?
explanation: The Service Trust Portal holds security, privacy and compliance content.

q: What do you need to open some Service Trust Portal compliance materials?
options: A Microsoft Entra work or school account and acceptance of the NDA
An Owner role on a subscription
explanation: Some content requires signing in and accepting Microsoft's non-disclosure agreement.

q: Which tool is an AI assistant that helps with Azure operations tasks such as drafting commands?
explanation: Copilot in Azure is an AI assistant. Always validate its suggestions.

q: Which declarative language is simpler and more concise than JSON ARM templates?
explanation: Bicep deploys through Azure Resource Manager with simpler syntax.

q: Which THREE can Azure Arc manage outside Azure? (Choose three)
explanation: Arc manages servers, Kubernetes clusters, Azure data services and SQL Server outside Azure.

q: Which view shows the global health of Azure across all services and regions?
explanation: Azure status is global. Service Health is personalised. Resource Health is for one resource.

q: Which Application Insights feature sends synthetic requests to check that your app is responding?
explanation: Availability tests probe your app even during low traffic.

q: Action groups can be reused by which services?
options: Azure Monitor, Service Health and Azure Advisor
explanation: Action groups are reusable across Monitor, Service Health and Advisor.

q: Batch jobs that can restart if interrupted are best suited to which pricing option?
explanation: Spot uses spare capacity at a discount but can be evicted.

q: Adding resources to the pricing calculator provisions them and you may be charged.
explanation: No. Nothing is provisioned and you are never charged. It only estimates.

q: In which two models is the customer responsible for the operating system? (Choose two)
explanation: You manage the OS on-premises and in IaaS. In PaaS and SaaS the provider manages it.

q: Select the answer that completes the sentence. [Answer choice] is the model where you supply your data and configure access, and the provider runs everything else.
explanation: SaaS: the provider manages the application stack. You manage your data and access settings.

q: Azure virtual networks belong to which cloud service type?
explanation: Virtual networks, VMs and storage are building blocks of IaaS.

q: Which Azure service is a PaaS offering?
explanation: App Service is PaaS. VMs and virtual networks are IaaS. Microsoft 365 is SaaS.

q: Which two tasks does the provider handle in a PaaS model? (Choose two)
explanation: The provider maintains the OS, middleware and runtime. You supply the code and the data.

q: A team wants a ready-made expense-tracking application with nothing to install or maintain. Which model fits best?
explanation: Finished applications such as finance and expense tracking are SaaS.

q: Which two are examples of scalability? (Choose two)
options: Adding RAM to a virtual machine
Adding more virtual machines when traffic rises
Applying tags to a resource group
explanation: Scaling up (more RAM or CPU) and scaling out (more instances) are the two kinds of scaling.

q: Which two are part of Azure's management infrastructure? (Choose two)
explanation: Management infrastructure covers resources, resource groups, subscriptions and management groups. Zones and region pairs are physical infrastructure.

q: Which two services can run containers? (Choose two)
explanation: ACI and AKS run containers. Azure Container Apps does as well.

q: Which two connections to Azure use an encrypted tunnel over the public internet? (Choose two)
explanation: VPN Gateway connections are encrypted tunnels over the internet. ExpressRoute and peering don't cross the public internet.

q: Which two are features of Microsoft Cost Management? (Choose two)
explanation: Cost Management offers cost analysis, budgets and cost alerts.

q: Which two tools help you govern Azure resources? (Choose two)
explanation: Azure Policy and resource locks are governance tools. The calculator estimates cost and Application Insights monitors apps.

q: Which two are views in Azure Service Health? (Choose two)
explanation: Azure status, Service Health and Resource Health are the three views.

q: Which two are Zero Trust principles? (Choose two)
explanation: Verify explicitly, use least privilege access and assume breach.

q: Which two redundancy options copy data across availability zones? (Choose two)
explanation: ZRS and GZRS both keep copies across three availability zones in the primary region.

q: Which two can you use to script Azure management tasks? (Choose two)
explanation: Azure CLI (Bash-style) and Azure PowerShell (cmdlets) are both scriptable.

q: Select the answer that correctly completes the sentence. [Answer choice] lets you deploy apps to regional datacenters around the world so users get the best performance in their region.
explanation: Deploying apps and data to regional datacenters worldwide is geo-distribution. High availability is about uptime.

q: A company rents virtual machines and wants to choose and patch the operating system itself. Which service model is this?
explanation: You manage the OS in IaaS (and on-premises). The provider manages it in PaaS and SaaS.

q: Which Azure object is the logical container used to combine and organise resources?
explanation: Resources are combined into resource groups. ARM is the deployment and management service.

q: A storage account named storage001 is an example of what?
explanation: Storage accounts, VMs, databases and virtual networks are resources.

q: Which two are typical jobs for Azure Blob storage? (Choose two)
options: Delivering images or documents straight to a web browser
Mounting a shared drive on many virtual machines
Providing the hard drive of a virtual machine
explanation: Blob serves files to browsers and stores backups. Azure Files gives a mountable shared drive, and Azure Disk is a VM drive.

q: A new team member must manage every resource inside one resource group and nothing else. Which Azure feature do you use?
explanation: RBAC assigns a role at a scope such as a resource group.

q: Several protective layers sit between an attacker and your data, and each layer slows the attack. What is this approach called?
explanation: Defense in depth uses several layers. The perimeter is only one of them.

q: You need to associate costs with different groups in your organisation without changing where the resources are. What should you use?
explanation: Tags group billing data without moving anything.

q: Several production VMs have steady usage all year. What minimises cost without reducing functionality?
explanation: Reservations discount stable, predictable workloads. Spot VMs can be evicted.

q: Your Linux admins prefer working in a Bash terminal to manage Azure resources. Which tool fits best?
explanation: The Azure CLI uses Bash-style commands. PowerShell uses PowerShell cmdlets.

q: Where do you find the official root cause analysis (RCA) report for an outage?
explanation: After an outage, Service Health provides official RCA incident reports.

q: What should you review and act on before service retirements or breaking changes interrupt you?
explanation: Health advisories need proactive action. Service issues are outages needing immediate action.
